data.summary: The top 1% of US businesses now allocate a record $10,199 per employee monthly on AI, more than tripling since January 2026, according to Ramp data across 85,000 companies. The top 10% spend $801 per employee, up 180% this year, while the median firm pays just $16—a 164% rise—with AI adoption reaching 56.8% of Ramp users. This concentration among venture-backed tech, finance, and services firms highlights a growing divide, as the enterprise AI market heads toward $155 billion by 2030 and worldwide spending nears $4 trillion in 2027.

data.hook: Workers at the San Francisco robotics startup arrived at payday on October 30 expecting their checks, only to learn the funds weren't there.
data.name: Foundation Future Industries Misses Payroll, Employees Go Unpaid
data.summary: Foundation Future Industries, backed by Eric Trump as an investor, failed to meet its October 30 payroll, leaving employees unpaid into mid-November. The cash crunch follows a $4.6 million company loan to CEO Sankaet Pathak last year for a luxury Sausalito home, a move approved without independent oversight as Pathak is the sole board member and majority shareholder. The firm, which builds military humanoid robots and seeks funding at a $3 billion valuation, also delayed August paychecks and faces governance concerns amid Pathak's past with the collapsed fintech Synapse.
